findings.passage: “My bill would have made it a felony to knowingly submit another person’s name or personal identity information on a ballot application or attempt to obtain multiple ballots.
findings.note: Senate caucus statement in his name, responding to the governor's veto of his bills on false identity information on absentee ballot applications. He describes the bill's purpose.

findings.passage: “I was very surprised to see the governor veto legislation that would have given Michiganders confidence in the security of their votes as we approach this unusual election.
findings.note: Same statement; he says the vetoed bill would have raised confidence in vote security.

findings.passage: “With the secretary of state’s recent decision to mail absentee ballot request forms to every name on their lists, we need to increase efforts that ensure our elections are not compromised.”
findings.note: Quoted in a Senate caucus release on the day the Senate passed his bills (SB 977 and 978) making it a felony to submit another person's identity information on a ballot application. He ties the bills to the mass mailing of absentee ballot request forms.

findings.passage: “This is a good step toward decreasing illegal activity and protecting the integrity and security of our votes.
findings.note: Same release; his comment on SB 977 and 978.

findings.passage: “Voting is the foundation of our system of government, and people need to have confidence in the results and that their elections are being conducted honestly.
findings.note: Statement issued after oversight committees voted to subpoena election records. General election-integrity comment; does not name ID or citizenship.

findings.passage: “It is our duty to restore faith in the election process and I believe these bills will spur a meaningful change in our state.”
findings.note: His quote in a release about an election reform package that, per the release, includes photo identification for in-person voting and with an absentee ballot application.
subjects: photo ID with absentee ballot application

findings.motion: 2021 election reform package of over 30 bills, sponsored/introduced with other senators, referred to the Senate Elections Committee
findings.note: Release says he joined other lawmakers in introducing the package. The release says it includes requiring photo identification for in-person voting and when submitting an absentee ballot application, cleaning up outdated voter lists, and barring mass mailing of absentee applications. The release does not list which of the bills carry his name.
subjects: photo ID with absentee ballot application
